claude.sample_unit: clinical scenarios (270 internal questions plus 30 external questions)

links.outcome: Expert-rated hallucination rate with guideline-grounded GraphRAG versus vanilla LLM and standard RAG
links.effect: Hallucination fell to 3.3% with EyeRAG vs 30.0% for Vanilla LLM; Naive RAG 16.6%, Hypothetical RAG 10.0%, Hierarchical Index RAG 6.6%.
links.quote: EyeRAG achieved the lowest observed hallucination rate, decreasing to 3.3% compared with 30.0% for Vanilla LLM.

links.outcome: EyeRAG performance across generation temperatures 0 to 1.0
links.effect: EyeRAG average ranks ranged from 1.45 ± 0.89 at temperature 0 to 1.78 ± 1.12 at temperature 1.0, consistently outperforming other RAG variants and vanilla LLM (3.67–4.23).
links.quote: EyeRAG maintained superior performance across all settings, with average ranks ranging from 1.45 ± 0.89 at temperature 0 to 1.78 ± 1.12 at temperature 1.0, consistently outperforming other RAG variants and the Vanilla LLM (which ranged from 3.67 ± 0.78 to 4.23 ± 0.95).

links.outcome: Performance on external hospital dataset versus internal dataset
links.effect: EyeRAG average rank 1.72 ± 1.18 externally vs 1.61 ± 1.04 internally; ranked first in 40.37% vs 40.29% of cases.
links.quote: EyeRAG maintained its superior performance, achieving an average rank of 1.72 ± 1.18—comparable to its 1.61 ± 1.04 in the primary ‘Overall Performance and Rankings’ evaluation (Fig. 4A )—and was ranked first in 40.37% of cases, on par with its 40.29% in the larger primary set.

links.outcome: Vanilla LLM clinical accuracy and safety versus retrieval-augmented systems
links.effect: Vanilla LLM fell significantly short in Clinical Accuracy and Safety; expert clinical accuracy/safety for EyeRAG was 2.98 on a 1-3 scale, total score 2.91 vs 1.32 for Vanilla LLM.
links.quote: The Vanilla LLM fell significantly short in Clinical Accuracy and Safety, highlighting the risks associated with its use in a clinical context without the safeguards provided by retrieval augmentation.

links.outcome: Agreement between LLM-as-a-judge and expert ophthalmologist rankings
links.effect: Kendall's W was 1.000 among experts, 0.956 among LLM judges, and 0.829 across combined expert and LLM-as-a-judge rankings.
links.quote: There was strong agreement across the combined expert and LLM-as-a-judge rankings, with a Kendall’s W of 0.829 (Friedman test, P < 0.001).

openai.sample_unit: generated patient questions from 120 clinical scenarios

links.effect: Expert total score: EyeRAG 2.91±0.11 vs Vanilla 1.32±0.22; Naive 1.81±0.26, Hypothetical 2.56±0.26, Hierarchical 2.68±0.26.
links.quote: As shown in Fig. 7 , EyeRAG achieved the highest mean total score of 2.91 ± 0.11, significantly outperforming Vanilla LLM (1.32 ± 0.22; p < 0.001, Dunn’s test), Naive RAG (1.81 ± 0.26; p < 0.001), Hypothetical RAG (2.56 ± 0.26; p < 0.01), and Hierarchical Index RAG (2.68 ± 0.26; p < 0.05).

links.effect: External rank 1.72±1.18 vs internal 1.61±1.04; first-ranked 40.37% vs 40.29%.
links.quote: EyeRAG maintained its superior performance, achieving an average rank of 1.72 ± 1.18—comparable to its 1.61 ± 1.04 in the primary ‘Overall Performance and Rankings’ evaluation (Fig. 4A )—and was ranked first in 40.37% of cases, on par with its 40.29% in the larger primary set.

links.effect: Across temperatures 0–1.0, EyeRAG rank ranged 1.45±0.89 to 1.78±1.12; Vanilla LLM 3.67±0.78 to 4.23±0.95.
links.quote: EyeRAG maintained superior performance across all settings, with average ranks ranging from 1.45 ± 0.89 at temperature 0 to 1.78 ± 1.12 at temperature 1.0, consistently outperforming other RAG variants and the Vanilla LLM (which ranged from 3.67 ± 0.78 to 4.23 ± 0.95).

links.effect: EyeRAG hallucination rate was 3.3% versus 30.0% for Vanilla LLM.
links.quote: EyeRAG achieved the lowest observed hallucination rate, decreasing to 3.3% compared with 30.0% for Vanilla LLM.

links.effect: Audit of 200 entities and 200 relationships found 100% guideline-presence precision and 100% description accuracy.
links.quote: The audit yielded 100% precision for guideline presence and 100% accuracy for descriptions, with no errors detected.
